Theorem
[Method of continuity criterion]1. ch17:17.7\group chapter-17 Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0460 Assume that $F$ is continuously differentiable on $E$, that each derivative $F_u$ for $u\in E$ is invertible, and that $S$ is closed in $[0,1]$. Then $F[u]=0$ is solvable for some $u\in \mathcal U$.
Proof

\sketch The set $S$ is nonempty because $1\in S$. Theorem 20 makes it open, while it is closed by hypothesis; hence $S=[0,1]$, and $0\in S$ gives the solution.

□

For (17.1) acting from $C^{2,\alpha }(\overline\Omega )$ to $C^\alpha (\overline\Omega )$, its derivative is \begin{equation} \tag {17.22} F_uh=F_{ij}D_{ij}h+F_{p_i}D_i h+F_zh, \end{equation} with every coefficient evaluated at $(x,u,Du,D^2u)$.
